sections.h2: Babies swallow solid mini-tablets better than syrup in trials

chart.title: Solid mini-tablets beat syrup by 10 and 14.8 points in infant trials
chart.sub: Gain of the mini-tablet over syrup, percentage points.
chart.source: Klingmann et al., J Pediatr 2013 and 2015 (PubMed abstracts).

sections.means: Uncoated mini-tablets were accepted better than syrup in a 2013 trial of 306 children, and newborns swallowed them better in 2015.
sections.todo: Prescribers and manufacturers should offer solid mini-tablets or films, tested for acceptability, as the first alternative to syrup for infants.

sections.h2: Cough-syrup labels for under-fours have moved from advice to binding rules

chart.title: Each step since 2023 has tightened the warning on cough-syrup labels
events: Regulator asks for a not-for-under-four label on the chlorpheniramine and phenylephrine combination
A notification makes the under-four warning binding
Health Ministry advises that cough and cold medicines should not go to children under two
Ministry extends the under-four warning to every formulation with the two drugs
Drugs Consultative Committee agrees in principle on red labels with no images of infants

sections.means: India's warnings have been extended step by step, and the labelling rules had not been amended by early November.
sections.todo: Regulators should amend the labelling rules to carry the agreed red under-four warning and drop images of infants or toddlers.

sections.h2: Almost half of infant melatonin ingestions involved gummies

chart.title: Gummies were involved in 47% of infant and toddler melatonin visits
chart.sub: Share of melatonin-related emergency visits by infants and young children, 2019 to 2022, %.
rows: Melatonin share of all unsupervised-ingestion visits

sections.means: Melatonin was involved in about 11,000 emergency visits by infants and young children in 2019 to 2022, and 47% of those cases involved gummies.
sections.todo: Parents and carers should keep melatonin and any sweet-shaped medicine out of children's reach, and the same logic argues against medicated lollipops for babies.
